clue.text: Important question of the elder offspring?

parts.note: at school the elder of two brothers is called major, as in Smith major
issue is a formal word for a person's children

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a big question concerns the firstborn child.
explanation.definitionFit: A significant matter for debate is a weighty topic, a big talking point.

clue.text: Being awkward, mean to get the last word

indicators.note: being awkward suggests the letters of the next word are put out of their natural order

explanation.surface: A contrary person is nasty in order to have the final say.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing word of a prayer or hymn is said at the very end, so it is the final utterance.

indicators.note: after places the musical note at the end, behind the rearranged bouts
punishing suggests the following word is knocked about into a fresh order

parts.note: E is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: A boxer is left slow-witted after some punishing fights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' could be any musical letter A to G; the answer's ending fixes it as E.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone slow to understand is dim, lacking sharpness of mind.

clue.text: I will shortly become accustomed to being maltreated

parts.note: I will contracted is I'll, written without its apostrophe
used to something means accustomed to it

explanation.surface: Someone resigns themselves to getting used to rough treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Treated badly or abused is the sense, the opposite of well looked after.

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word said aloud gives the letters entered

parts.note: a sight is something seen, a view

explanation.surface: A tourist spot worth seeing, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A location or spot where something stands or happens.

indicators.note: thrown suggests the letters of grenade are tossed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone hurls a bomb in a fit of rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Being furious means being in a temper, angry and worked up.

parts.note: reads like a glance at the speedometer, but check means curb, so it is slowing down

explanation.surface: A driver glances at the speedometer.
explanation.definitionFit: To slow down is to rein in velocity, reducing the pace of travel.

clue.text: You may get it in the neck when you detain the boss

definitions.text: You may get it in the neck

parts.note: to collar someone is to grab or arrest them
a boss is a raised knob, also called a stud

explanation.surface: Grabbing your employer could land you in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' wants to be an employer; here it is the ornamental knob on a surface. 'Get it in the neck' means to be punished, but the item literally fastens at the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: This small fastener fixes a detachable shirt neckband, so it sits at the throat.

clue.text: Famous Italian seen back in Florence

indicators.note: back says the run of letters found is read from right to left
in shows the letters sit inside the word Florence

explanation.surface: A celebrated Italian is spotted returning to Florence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds OREN inside Florence and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor said to have fiddled while Rome burned is a notorious Italian figure.

definitions.meaning: a fan is a device that moves air around a room
a hospital machine that helps a sick patient breathe, playing on the welfare payment

explanation.surface: Someone is a keen supporter of welfare payments for the ill.
explanation.definitionFit: An air-circulating device, or a breathing machine aiding patients in intensive care.

definitions.meaning: to ask earnestly for something, as in a plea
a request to a higher court to reconsider a verdict

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a wiser decision.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea or request, and also a legal application for review by a higher court.

clue.text: Reported to be held at gun-point

definitions.meaning: journalists who report an event are said to cover it
a gunman who has someone in his sights has them ...

explanation.surface: Word is that someone was held hostage at gun-point.
explanation.definitionFit: Reported on by the press, or kept under the aim of a weapon.

definitions.meaning: something told in private trust, as in telling someone a secret
trust or faith, as in having faith in someone

explanation.surface: A secret held in common becomes a conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: A private disclosure entrusted to someone, and also trust or self-assurance.

parts.note: everyday local language as people actually speak it, as opposed to formal or literary forms

explanation.definitionFit: The everyday dialect of ordinary people, rather than formal or written language.

clue.text: Old-fashioned but popular with the boys

definitions.meaning: out of date, no longer current
a girl taken out by many boyfriends has gone on many romantic outings

explanation.surface: A girl is out of fashion yet still a hit with young men.
explanation.definitionFit: Outmoded, and also past tense of going out romantically with someone.

clue.text: Old master of the Exchange Rate Mechanism in turn-about

indicators.note: in places the economic abbreviation within the word for a change of direction

parts.note: to veer is to change direction sharply
ERM is the standard abbreviation for the European Exchange Rate Mechanism

explanation.surface: A great painter is linked to a U-turn over European currency policy.
explanation.walkthrough: The ERM was the European currency system Britain left in 1992; 'turn-about' recalls that U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Old masters are great European painters before about 1800, and this Dutch painter is one.

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of drive are set off course into a new order

explanation.surface: A leading batsman hits an off-drive in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: An off-drive is a cricket shot, and a top scorer seems a batsman; here a scorer writes musical scores. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading Italian opera composer is a great writer of musical scores.

clue.text: Ventured again to take father out

indicators.note: out says the word for father stands outside, round the other piece

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father
re- is a prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: Someone plucks up courage a second time to take their dad out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a night out with Dad; 'out' is really the container signal, with father wrapped around the prefix for again.
explanation.definitionFit: Had the courage to do something risky, took a chance.

parts.note: arresting suggests striking news, but the tip-off is what lets police make an arrest

explanation.definitionFit: A police informer passes on tip-offs leading to arrests.

parts.note: looks like a nursery for toddlers, but it is the company of actors in a play

explanation.definitionFit: The actors appearing together in a dramatic production form a company.

definitions.meaning: to yield or give way, as in bowing to pressure
decompression sickness, caused by surfacing too fast

explanation.surface: Someone gives in to a scuba diver's ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Gives way or yields, and also decompression sickness suffered by divers.

indicators.note: interrupts says one piece breaks into the middle of another

parts.note: a brawl is a rough fight
an ad is a commercial or advertisement

explanation.surface: A dull television advert breaks into a punch-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' suggests dull; here it means making holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pointed hand implement for making holes in wood.

parts.note: outstanding read as standing out in the cold, a figure built in the garden after snowfall

explanation.definitionFit: A figure built from packed snow stands outdoors in winter.

clue.text: Briefly, I draw no new conclusion

indicators.note: a new conclusion suggests the letters of the preceding words are worked into a different outcome

explanation.surface: In short, someone refuses to reach a fresh verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something in short or in summary, using as few words as possible.

clue.text: A change in dates offered as an alternative

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a change says the letters of dates are rearranged

explanation.surface: A different date is proposed as a fallback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like part of the anagram signal 'A change in', but it supplies its own two letters at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: In place of something else, as a substitute.

parts.note: high-handedness reads as arrogance, but means the clock's hands are both pointing straight up

explanation.definitionFit: At noon or midnight both clock hands point to the top of the dial.

indicators.note: potential suggests the letters of duel could become something else

explanation.surface: A journalist dodged a possible duel with his editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Escaped or dodged, as in evading capture.

indicators.note: break says the word case is broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Detectives crack the case.
explanation.definitionFit: Highly skilled people are stars or masters at what they do.

clue.text: Name expert seen about skin problem

indicators.note: seen about says the word for expert goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A specialist dermatologist is named for a skin complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Spots and pimples on the face, a common complaint of adolescence.

clue.text: Oddly comic place associated with criminal

indicators.note: oddly suggests the letters of comic place are arranged in a strange way

explanation.surface: A strange comedy club is linked to a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' rearranges COMIC PLACE; 'associated with' is a link but hints at a partner in crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner in crime, someone who helps commit an offence, is a lawbreaker.

definitions.meaning: to pack tightly, as in filling a bag
to revise intensively just before a test

explanation.surface: A student revises frantically before a test.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack something tightly, and to revise hurriedly for a test.

clue.text: Long leases needed for a place to live in America

definitions.text: a place to live in America

indicators.note: needed suggests the letters of long leases are kneaded, worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Lengthy property leases are required for a home in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed' rearranges LONG LEASES, perhaps punning on kneaded.
explanation.definitionFit: A large Californian city is somewhere one might settle in the United States.
